about: I'm a PhD student at the Gran Sasso Science Institute (GSSI) in L'Aquila, Italy. My main research field of interest is experimental particle physics, with a focus on direct Dark Matter detection. I'm a member of the DarkSide collaboration working on the DarkSide-20k experiment, currently under construction at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS).
When I'm not doing physics you'll usually find me hiking or playing the guitar and do a lot of other stuff.

research.lead: I search for dark matter, the invisible substance that dominates the matter content of the Universe.

topics.title: Hunting dark matter with DarkSide-20k
topics.body: I work on DarkSide-20k, a next-generation dual-phase liquid-argon time projection chamber searching for WIMP dark matter at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso. A dark matter particle would reveal itself as a tiny flash of light and a handful of ionization electrons — and the whole experiment is built to catch it against an almost perfectly quiet background.

topics.title: Reading the light: SiPM photo-sensors
topics.body: The detector sees through thousands of silicon photomultipliers grouped into Photon Detection Units. I characterize their response — in particular the cross-talk and afterpulse probabilities extracted from the charge spectrum — and build the baseline-reconstruction and real-time data-acquisition tools that turn their raw signals into physics.

topics.title: A sense of direction: CYGNO
topics.body: Before DarkSide, I worked on CYGNO, which reads out a gas TPC optically to reconstruct the direction of a nuclear recoil — the directional signature that would be a smoking gun for a genuine galactic dark matter signal.
topics.citation_text: CYGNO Collaboration, Modeling the light response of an optically read-out GEM-based TPC for the CYGNO experiment, arXiv:2505.06362 (2025).

talks.title: Cross-talk & afterpulse extraction from the SiPM charge spectrum

cv.award: 2nd place — GWOSC Data Challenge (2023). Ranked 2nd of ~500 participants worldwide in gravitational-wave signal analysis on LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA data.
